Detail: Score card transactions for fraud risk in real time; route to approve, step-up or decline
ULB/Worldline European card transactions, Sept. 2013; 284,807 rows, 492 frauds (0.173%); Dal Pozzolo et al. (2015)
Chronological 80/20: 227,845 development (417 frauds) / 56,962 test (75 frauds); 5-fold walk-forward validation
XGBoost, 400 trees, depth 4, learning rate 0.05, subsample 0.8, scale_pos_weight 545, seed 42
Logistic regression PR-AUC 0.752; Isolation Forest PR-AUC 0.039
0.54, cost-minimizing on walk-forward scores at $15 per false alarm (assumption)
TP 57, FN 18, FP 17, TN 56870; cost $2,893 vs $7,729 with no model (62.6% reduction)
Step-up at 0.19, decline at 0.86; net cost $3,202 (assumes 90% step-up stop rate)
Single transaction median 0.77 ms, p99 1.10 ms; budget 100 ms (arm64)
TreeSHAP reason codes per decision; top global features V4, V14, V12
Recall by amount quartile: Q1 84%, Q2 55%, Q3 78%, Q4 72% (small fraud counts)
PR-AUC by window: T1 0.87, T2 0.79, T3 0.89, T4 0.55

Anonymized PCA features (no feature engineering or plain-language reasons); no demographics, so fairness is a proxy; two days of 2013 data; no Time column (row order used); results vary slightly by hardware
Recommended: drift-triggered retraining, independent validation and audit trail (SR 26-2)
